audits.title: Audit of open tibial diaphyseal fracture management at a district accident centre.
audits.standard: BOA and BAPS guidelines: first orthopaedic procedure within 6 h; soft tissue cover within 5 days
audits.setting: Royal Preston Hospital, district accident centre with on-site plastic and orthopaedic units

cycle1.result: 74% had first orthopaedic procedure within 6 h; 50% had soft tissue cover within 5 days.

audits.intervention: Changes in practice (not specified in abstract).

cycle2.result: 80% had first orthopaedic procedure within 6 h; all had soft tissue cover within 5 days.

audits.other_findings: 8% of injuries undergraded by Gustilo at surgery; 5% required fasciotomy for compartment syndrome.
audits.citation: Clough TM, Bale RS. Audit of open tibial diaphyseal fracture management at a district accident centre. Ann R Coll Surg Engl. 2000;82(6):436-440. PMID: 11103167.

audits.title: A representative assessment of the management of open fractures of the lower limb within UK orthoplastic centres: A two-centre audit of compliance with national standards.
audits.standard: BOAST 4 (BAPRAS/BOA) and NICE guidance: debridement within 24h, soft tissue cover within 72h and 7 days
audits.setting: Orthoplastic units, Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital and Royal Stoke University Hospital

cycle1.result: Debridement within 24h 83 (98.8%); plastic surgeon at 33.3% of initial operations; soft tissue cover within 72h 56.4% and within 7 days 78.2% (of 78).

audits.other_findings: Of 42 out-of-hours initial operations only 10 (23.8%) had an urgent indication.
audits.citation: Rymer B, Dimovska EOF, Chou DTS, Choa R, Davis B, Huq S. A representative assessment of the management of open fractures of the lower limb within UK orthoplastic centres: A two-centre audit of compliance with national standards. Injury. 2017;48(10):2266-2269. doi:10.1016/j.injury.2017.07.012. PMID: 28729006.

audits.title: Clínical Audit of Primary Treatment of Open Fractures: Antibiotic Treatment and Tetanus Prophylaxis.
audits.standard: Institutional Clinical Protocol 'Primary Treatment of Exposed Fractures' (FHEMIG, 2014): preoperative antibiotics; regimen by Gustilo type (cefazolin 1 g IV 6-hourly ± gentamicin 240 mg daily ± metronidazole 500 mg 6-hourly); duration 24 hours for types I and II and 72 hours for type III; tetanus prophylaxis according to vaccination history
audits.setting: Hospital João XXIII (Fundação Hospitalar de Minas Gerais), state public hospital specialised in urgency and trauma, Belo Horizonte

cycle1.result: Preoperative antibiotics prescribed in 221 (91.7%); 59.3% (99/167) received a regimen not recommended by the protocol; 58.0% (254/438) of antibiotic doses were inconsistent; 63.5% of courses had an inadequate duration (95.6% of type I and II given > 24 hours); only 34 (14.1%) patients immunised against tetanus and vaccination history missing in 207 (85.9%).

audits.other_findings: Gustilo classification was not recorded in 39.4% of patients; infection occurred in 18.7% and was associated with type III fractures, postoperative antibiotic start and antibiotics started more than 3 hours after admission. Mean time to surgery was 4 hours 12 minutes, with 82.6% operated within 6 hours.
audits.citation: Assunção ALF, Oliveira de ST. Clínical Audit of Primary Treatment of Open Fractures: Antibiotic Treatment and Tetanus Prophylaxis. Rev Bras Ortop (Sao Paulo). 2020;55(3):284-292. doi:10.1055/s-0039-3402470. PMID: 32616972.

audits.title: National Metrics Improved Timeliness of Antibiotic Administration for Open Extremity Fractures.
audits.standard: American College of Surgeons Trauma Quality Improvement Program best-practice guidelines: antibiotic order and administration within 1 hour
audits.setting: Single institution (authors at University of California Davis Medical Center, Sacramento)

cycle1.result: Baseline period; figures not given in abstract.

audits.intervention: First, institutional awareness and education of departments; second, tracking of antibiotic order and administration times with quarterly audits following new guidelines.

cycle2.result: Antibiotic order within 1 hour and administration within 1 hour both significantly improved after the second initiative, as did median arrival-to-order and arrival-to-administration times (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Three periods were compared; neither measure improved after the first, education-only initiative.
audits.citation: Shieh AK, Lucas JF, Shelton TJ, Wright AJ, Steffner RJ, Wolinsky PR. National Metrics Improved Timeliness of Antibiotic Administration for Open Extremity Fractures. J Orthop Trauma. 2021;35(8):437-441. doi:10.1097/bot.0000000000002027. PMID: 33278206.

audits.title: Open lower limb fractures in the UK trauma system: A multicentre prospective audit of current practice.
audits.standard: BOA and BAPRAS standards for trauma (open fractures)
audits.setting: 3 major trauma centres and 5 trauma units

cycle1.result: Antibiotics within 1 hour 41.7%; splint in ED 74.4%; documented orthoplastic plan 85.8%; debridement within 12 hours for high-energy injuries 41.7%

audits.other_findings: 42.3% of patients were managed at some point in a trauma unit.

audits.title: A retrospective analysis of the definitive management of open talus fractures at a major trauma centre, comparing ORIF to FUSION: cohort study and audit of BOAST 4 guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST 4 guidelines for open fractures (e.g. prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury, definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h, orthoplastic involvement, debridement); no target stated
audits.setting: Addenbrooke's Major Trauma Unit, Cambridge University Hospitals; major trauma centre, open talus fractures in skeletally mature patients

cycle1.result: 15 open talus fractures in 14 patients. 100% had orthoplastic involvement, initial saline-soaked gauze and occlusive film dressing, functional recovery and rehabilitation advice, and recorded debridement; 60% had debridement using fasciotomy lines. Only 27% received prophylactic antibiotics within one hour of injury and only 27% achieved definitive soft tissue coverage within 72 h (mean 9.7 days in the 7 needing coverage).

audits.other_findings: Mainly a cohort comparison: no significant difference between ORIF and tibiocalcaneal fusion in EQ-5D-5L (p = 0.13), FAAM-ADL (p = 0.20), FAAM-Sport (p = 0.34) or infection rate (p = 0.55); deep infection occurred in 7 cases (47%).
audits.citation: Zhou AK, Jou E, Patel R, Bhatti F, Modi N, Lu V, et al.. A retrospective analysis of the definitive management of open talus fractures at a major trauma centre, comparing ORIF to FUSION: cohort study and audit of BOAST 4 guidelines. Eur J Orthop Surg Traumatol. 2023;33(2):393-400. doi:10.1007/s00590-022-03204-3. PMID: 35031854.

audits.title: Orthoplastics Management of Open Lower Limb Fractures at a Major Trauma Centre: Audit of Adherence to BOAST4 Guidelines.
audits.standard: BOAST 4 open lower limb fracture standards, e.g. IV antibiotics within 1 h of injury; debridement within 12 h for high-energy and 24 h for other fractures; definitive soft tissue cover within 72 h; gentamicin on induction; photographs; saline lavage
audits.setting: Major Trauma Centre for the South East of England, University Hospitals Sussex NHS Foundation Trust, Brighton; orthoplastic service

cycle1.result: Debridement within 24 h 81% (108/133); high-energy within 12 h 25% (15/60); mean time to first debridement 18.77 h. Definitive fixation/closure within 72 h 75% (95). Prehospital antibiotics within 1 h 76% (87/115); neurovascular documentation 94% (120/128); realignment and splinting 51% (45/89); photographs 86% (115); gentamicin on induction 65% (87); saline wash documented 78% (104).

audits.other_findings: Post-operative infection rate 13% (16 patients); prehospital antibiotics within 1 h associated with lower infection (p<0.001). Documentation of prehospital care and intraoperative steps was frequently missing; authors recommend referral and operation note proformas and training.
audits.citation: Lacey H, Bernard K, Syed L, O'Rourke E, Calvert-Ford Y, Bovis J, et al.. Orthoplastics Management of Open Lower Limb Fractures at a Major Trauma Centre: Audit of Adherence to BOAST4 Guidelines. JPRAS Open. 2024;42:133-145. doi:10.1016/j.jpra.2024.08.003. PMID: 39308745.

audits.title: Microlearning Reduces Unnecessary Antibiotic Provision for Open Hand Injuries.
audits.standard: BSSH Hand Trauma App guidance and local OUH guidelines on indications for antibiotics in open hand injuries
audits.setting: Plastic surgery acute referrals (OARS), Oxford University Hospitals NHS teaching trust

cycle1.result: 22/44 (50.0%) referrals without an indication were given or advised antibiotics; 10/84 (12%) with an indication were neither given nor advised antibiotics.

audits.intervention: Infographic poster displayed and emailed to resident doctors (PDSA 1), then a short microlearning video shared on WhatsApp and email (PDSA 2).

cycle2.result: 5/35 (14.3%) without an indication given or advised antibiotics (p=0.002 vs baseline).

audits.other_findings: After the infographic alone (25/7/22–31/7/22, n=52), 7/16 (43.8%) were given unnecessary antibiotics (not significant). Three of the five remaining cases were given antibiotics by the referrer before referral.
audits.citation: Armstrong EJ, Jamal A, Quinlan C. Microlearning Reduces Unnecessary Antibiotic Provision for Open Hand Injuries. Cureus. 2024;16(12):e74910. doi:10.7759/cureus.74910. PMID: 39624810.

audits.title: Scottish Open Fractures of Tibia (SOFT) audit; a multi-centre retrospective review of ortho-plastic management of tibial shaft fractures at major trauma centres (MTCs) in Scotland.
audits.setting: Major trauma centres across the four Scottish Trauma Networks (SOFT audit)

cycle1.result: Complete compliance with BOAST guidelines documented in 8.8% of cases.

audits.other_findings: Infection 24%, return to theatre 17%, soft-tissue failure 9.7%, amputation 7.1%; improvement needed in antibiotic timing, combined ortho-plastics approach and soft-tissue cover within 72 h.
audits.citation: Dixon JE, Rankin IA, Rangarajan S, Brennan J, Varma A, Shields DW, et al.. Scottish Open Fractures of Tibia (SOFT) audit; a multi-centre retrospective review of ortho-plastic management of tibial shaft fractures at major trauma centres (MTCs) in Scotland. Surgeon. 2025;23(2):87-93. doi:10.1016/j.surge.2025.01.006. PMID: 39875310.
